title: Safai Saathi custom claims
description: Every custom claim the platform mints. A claim is the ONLY thing the Firestore rules can use to tell one caller from another. The client never names its own scope. If a value in this file is missing from a token, every rule that depends on it denies. If a value is misspelled, the same happens and nothing says why.
x-principle: The client proves who it is with a claim that the server minted. The rules trust only the claim. Every decision that needs live state happens in a Function.

vanId.scope: The van the session is bound to. Scopes the driver's writes to vans and trips.

driverId.scope: The driver's badge code. Scopes the drivers doc read. This is the phone-number wall: without it, any signed-in caller can read any driver's phone.

currentTripId.scope: The open trip. Lets a complaint rule be a pure token check with no get().

deviceId.scope: The citizen's install id. Scopes the complaint and rating reads. Q6: same install only.

routeId.scope: The route the citizen's ward belongs to. Scopes the trip reads for the 'collected today' display.
routeId.refreshRule: Re-mint when the citizen's ward changes to one on a different route. A stale value shows the wrong neighbourhood, which is a UX annoyance, not a data leak.

role.scope: The staff role. Determines what they may act on.

staffId.scope: The staff doc id. The scope key for the admin panel.

wardIds.scope: The staff member's ward scope. In the token so the rules do not get() on every read.

x-minting.principle: A claim is minted only by the server, only from an authoritative document the client cannot edit. The client asks; the server answers.
never: A client parameter is never a claim. A client parameter is forgeable.
A badge code is never a claim. The badge code is public by design.
A deviceId sent in a query is never a scope. It must be in the token.

x-staleness.principle: A token's claims are a snapshot. A claim that is a privilege goes stale and must be checked against a live document before it is acted on.
x-staleness.privilegeExpiry: Firebase ID tokens expire after one hour. The client refreshes them. So a scope change lands within an hour.
x-staleness.instantRevocation: staff/{id}.active = false takes effect immediately, because every admin write goes through a callable that reads the live staff doc. See Q5 and ADR-0003.
